brief.headline: Cut laminate price from ₹1067.36/KG to ₹250/KG — we're paying 326.9% more than Silk Polypack for identical material.

priceAsk.summary: Ask them to match ₹250.00/KG, the price Silk Polypack charges us for the same laminate.
priceAsk.basis: Our current price is ₹1067.36/KG — a 326.9% gap above the ₹250.00/KG we pay Silk Polypack for identical material. The market fair-price band for pharma sachet laminate is ₹205–305/kg, and BOPET film import cost is 171.60 ₹/kg — so ₹250/KG sits at the top of the fair band and leaves room for conversion cost.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Ask to move from 30 days to immediate payment (or 15 days) in exchange for part of the price cut.
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Paying immediately frees up ₹6316 cash for us; paying 15 days earlier frees ₹3158.

brief.financialLeverage: Huhtamaki India publishes no financials, so we can't see their revenue, profit or cash position. Our ₹76850 annual spend with them is tiny — they're a large listed flexible-packaging company, so we're a drop in the bucket and have little spend leverage. That means our negotiating power comes entirely from the price gap, the proven alternate at ₹250/KG, and the threat of shifting volume to UFLEX or another converter if they won't move. Line up a second source now so the alternate is real, not a bluff.

evidence.point: We pay them ₹1067.36/KG for laminate — 326.9% more than the ₹250.00/KG Silk Polypack charges for the same thing.
Closing that gap saves us ₹58850 a year on this one SKU.
The open market for pharma sachet laminate runs ₹205–305/kg, with ₹250/kg typical — our ask sits at the top of the fair band.
Raw BOPET film imports cost about 171.60 ₹/kg — so ₹250/kg leaves roughly ₹78/kg for printing, lamination and margin.
Our annual spend with them is only ₹76850 — we're a very small customer.
Paying them immediately instead of at 30 days frees up ₹6316 cash for us.

alternates.name: UFLEX Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexibles giant that makes both film and converts laminates — can second-source our sachets at scale.

alternates.name: Constantia Parikh Packaging Pvt Ltd
alternates.why: Part of the global Constantia group, does pharma blister and sachet laminates; revenue ₹222.04 Cr, health score D (31/100) — a credible second source but watch credit.

alternates.name: Amcor Flexibles India Pvt Ltd
alternates.why: India arm of global Amcor — premium pharma laminates, very reliable (no health/revenue data, but brand strength is high).

risks: We're a tiny customer (₹76850 spend) — they may not care if we walk, so the alternate threat must be real and ready.
Huhtamaki's financials aren't public, so we can't gauge how desperate or comfortable they are — assume they're stable and won't move much without a firm RFQ to a second source.
The 326.9% gap is huge — if they won't come close to ₹250/KG, it signals either a quality/spec difference we missed or they've been overcharging us for years; either way, move volume fast.
Constantia Parikh has a low health score (D, 31/100) — qualify their credit and capacity carefully before shifting large orders.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We're paying you ₹1067 a kilo for laminate, but Silk Polypack does the same material at ₹250 — I'd like to understand the gap and work toward that benchmark today.
